user.title: Connect to the ABUS Secvest panel
user.description:
Tested with the {model} running firmware {firmware}; other panels and firmware versions are untested.

Use a separate panel user for Home Assistant: the level "normal user" is enough, with rights for exactly the partitions Home Assistant should operate. The installer code doesn't work, the panel's API accepts users only.

data_description.url: The panel's address, e.g. 192.168.1.10 (port 4433) or 192.168.1.10:4433, or the https URL of a reverse proxy in front of it.
data_description.user_code: The code of the panel user Home Assistant logs in with.
data_description.password: The password of that panel user.
data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off for the panel's own self-signed certificate; turn on behind a reverse proxy with a valid certificate.

data_description.user_agent: Sent with every request. Leave empty for the default, ha-secvest/ followed by the version; only needed for a reverse proxy that filters by User-Agent.

partitions.title: Select partitions
partitions.description:
Select the partitions Home Assistant should show and operate. Their zones are added automatically.

The panel doesn't reveal which partitions the user may operate, so all of them are listed; partitions without zones are deselected. Commands for a partition the user has no rights for are refused by the panel.

reauth_confirm.title: Reauthenticate
reauth_confirm.description: The panel rejected the user code or password for {name}. Nothing is sent to the panel with the old credentials anymore. Enter the credentials of the panel user again; they are checked with a single request.

data_description.user_code: The code of the panel user Home Assistant logs in with.
data_description.password: The password of that panel user.

zones.title: Zones
zones.description: Choose what kind of detector each zone is; the panel doesn't tell. Excluded zones get no entities. You can change this later in the integration's options. Zones that belong to one opening, such as the two wings of a window, can be combined afterwards with "Add zone group" on the integration's page. Add codes for arming and disarming there too ("Add code"); without one, the alarm panel can't arm or disarm.

data_description.excluded_zones: These zones are still read with their partition but get no entities or device.

error.invalid_address: Enter a host name or IP address, optionally with a port, or an https URL.
error.invalid_auth: The panel rejected the user code or password. Nothing is retried automatically; check the credentials and try again.
error.installer_locked: The installer is logged in at the panel, which locks the API. Try again after the installer has logged out.
error.cannot_connect: The panel could not be reached. Check the address and the network.
error.timeout: The panel did not answer in time. Check the address; the panel may be busy.
error.unexpected_response: The address answered, but not like a Secvest panel. Check the address (and the path behind a reverse proxy).

init.title: Options
init.description: Changes reload the integration. Nothing is sent to the panel here; the choices come from the last polling round.

data_description.partitions: The partitions Home Assistant shows and operates; their zones are added automatically.
data_description.scan_interval: How often the panel is polled, in seconds. Never below 24 seconds, the official app's own cycle.
data_description.log_interval: How often new entries of the panel's log are read, in seconds. At least 120 seconds: reading the log takes the panel several seconds.

data_description.user_agent: Sent with every request. Leave empty for the default, ha-secvest/ followed by the version; only needed for a reverse proxy that filters by User-Agent.

zones.title: Zones
zones.description: Choose what kind of detector each zone is; the panel doesn't tell. Excluded zones get no entities. Zones of a newly selected partition show their names after the next reload. Zones that belong to one opening, such as the two wings of a window, can be combined afterwards with "Add zone group" on the integration's page.

data_description.excluded_zones: These zones are still read with their partition but get no entities or device.

abort.not_loaded: The integration isn't loaded. Fix the problem shown for it first (for example reauthenticate), then change the options.

missing_partition.title: Partition {partition} not found
missing_partition.description: The panel of {name} no longer reports partition {partition}, which is selected in the integration's options. Its entities are unavailable. Open the integration's options and change the selection.

empty_partition.title: Partition {partition} has no zones
empty_partition.description: Partition {partition} of {name} is selected in the integration's options but has no zones anymore, so Home Assistant shows only its state and it can't be armed. If it stays empty, open the integration's options and deselect it; otherwise ignore this issue.

zone_group_zones_gone.title: Zone group {group} has zones that no longer exist
zone_group_zones_gone.description: The zone group {group} of {name} contains zones that the selected partitions no longer list: {zones}. The group sensor ignores them. If the zones were removed at the panel, open the integration's page, choose the group and reconfigure it; if you deselected their partition, select it again in the options. This issue disappears once the group fits again.

user.title: Add zone group
user.description: Combine zones that belong to one opening, e.g. the two wings of a window. The group gets its own device and a sensor that is on while any of its zones is open. The zones keep their own devices.

data_description.name: Used for the device ("Zone group" followed by the name) and the entity id.
data_description.zones: At least two zones; a zone can be in one group only.
data_description.device_class: How the group sensor is shown, e.g. window or door. "Same as the zones" takes the type the zones show and follows it.
data_description.hide_members: Hide the entities of the grouped zones in Home Assistant; they keep working and can still be used in automations.
data_description.area_id: The area of the group device. Can also be changed on the device page later.

reconfigure.title: Change zone group
reconfigure.description: Change the zones or settings of this group.

data_description.name: Used for the device ("Zone group" followed by the name); the entity id stays.
data_description.zones: At least two zones; a zone can be in one group only.
data_description.device_class: How the group sensor is shown, e.g. window or door. "Same as the zones" takes the type the zones show and follows it.
data_description.hide_members: Hide the entities of the grouped zones in Home Assistant; they keep working and can still be used in automations.
data_description.area_id: The area of the group device. Can also be changed on the device page later.

error.name_exists: A group with this name exists already.
error.zones_differ: The zones show different types; choose one.

abort.not_loaded: The integration isn't loaded. Fix the problem shown for it first, then change the zone groups.

user.title: Add code
user.description: A code for arming and disarming from Home Assistant. You may use the same four-digit codes as at the keypad; Home Assistant can't check them against the panel, so a code changed at the keypad has to be changed here too.

data_description.name: Shown as the one who armed or disarmed.

reconfigure.title: Change code
reconfigure.description: Change the user's name or code. Leave the code empty to keep it.

data_description.name: Shown as the one who armed or disarmed.
data_description.code: Four digits; empty keeps the current code.

error.name_exists: A code for this user exists already.
error.invalid_code: Enter a code of four digits.
error.code_exists: Another user has this code already.
